findings.title: Client removal now calls setPermissionsEnabled, which throws in V2
findings.body: The new ClientRemovedEvent branch calls management(...).clients().setPermissionsEnabled(client, false). When ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is on, management() returns MgmtPermissionsV2, and clients() now returns ClientPermissionsV2. Its setPermissionsEnabled() unconditionally throws UnsupportedOperationException (ClientPermissionsV2 line ~193). Deleting any client in a realm with V2 enabled and this listener active will therefore fail or roll back the deletion. The listener needs to skip or no-op for V2, or ClientPermissionsV2 must implement the cleanup.

findings.title: Possible NPE when the all-clients resource is missing
findings.body: In hasPermission(ClientModel, scope), if no per-client resource exists, the code loads the 'Clients' type resource via getResourceTypeResource(). That method returns null when the resource is not found. The next line then calls authz.getStoreFactory().getPolicyStore().findByResource(server, resource) with a null resource, which can NPE. Even if it doesn't, line 224 uses resource.getScopes() on null. A null check on resource should return false.

findings.title: canMapRoles and related methods ignore the MANAGE_CLIENTS realm role
findings.body: canManage(), canConfigure() and canView() all short-circuit when the caller has MANAGE_CLIENTS. canMapRoles, canMapCompositeRoles and canMapClientScopeRoles only check the schema permission via hasPermission(client, ...). Callers with the manage-clients admin role can therefore be denied role mapping on clients under V2, even though the V1 contract and the interface javadoc treat that role as granting access. Confirm this is intended, and add the role check if not.

findings.title: requireView() javadoc describes a boolean return instead of a throw
findings.body: The javadoc for requireView() says 'Returns true if canView() returns true', but the method is void and must throw ForbiddenException when access is denied. The same copy-paste error appears on several other require* methods in this interface, such as requireViewClientScopes. This misleads implementers about the contract.
